# Use the RasterFold C API

Include `rasterfold.h` and link one library from the matching target directory. The API is plain C11 with C++ linkage guards. `rf_version()` reports API 1.0 as `0x00010000`; the encoded file format has its own version, currently 2.

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `rf_version` | API major and minor version |
| `rf_encode_image` | An owned `.fold` byte buffer from RGB8 pixels |
| `rf_decode_image` | Owned, tightly packed RGB8 pixels from a complete `.fold` buffer |
| `rf_inspect` | Validated metadata after checking and decoding the complete file |
| `rf_free` | Releases an allocation returned by this loaded library |

## Ownership and concurrency

Input buffers are borrowed for the duration of a call. Encoding accepts top-down RGB8 with a stride of at least `width * 3`; `size` must cover the last row. Padding is ignored. Decoding returns packed pixels. Output structures must be distinct from the inputs, options and error structure, and must not contain an allocation you still need: calls initialize their outputs without freeing a previous value.

Release every returned allocation with `rf_free`, from the same loaded library that produced it. Do not use the caller's `free`, pass caller allocations to `rf_free`, or share allocations between separately loaded codec copies. `rf_free(NULL)` is allowed. The library never opens a file.

Calls with distinct outputs and error structures may run concurrently. Tables initialize once, and errors are per call. An error's message points to a static string inside the library; it is not owned by the caller and becomes invalid when the library is unloaded. Process-wide peak allocation statistics are diagnostic only and are not a per-call memory accounting API.

```c
#include "rasterfold.h"

rf_options options = { sizeof options, 1, {0} };
rf_pixels pixels = { width, height, stride, RF_LAYOUT_RGB8, rgb, rgb_size };
rf_buffer encoded = {0};
rf_error error = {0};
int result = rf_encode_image(&pixels, &options, &encoded, &error);
if (result == RF_OK) {
    /* Use encoded.data[0..encoded.size), then release it. */
    rf_free(encoded.data);
}
```

Initialize the options size field and reserved words as shown. `threads=0` selects automatic operation; 1 through 9 are accepted. A null options pointer selects defaults. The original eight-byte options prefix is accepted. Nonzero known reserved fields are refused, as are sizes above the library's known structure size or sizes that are not multiples of four. Thread count never changes file bytes.

## Linking

On Linux, the shared object has soname `librasterfold.so.1` and a development alias `librasterfold.so`. Link `librasterfold.so` with a runtime loader path appropriate to your application, or link `librasterfold.a` plus pthreads. Static means the codec is archived; it does not mean the entire program includes a static libc.

```bash
tools/llvm-mingw-linux/bin/clang --target=x86_64-linux-gnu \
  -Iinclude examples/encode.c bin/linux-x64/lib/librasterfold.a -pthread -o build/encode-example
```

On Windows, define `RF_SHARED` when importing the DLL and link `librasterfold.dll.a` with MinGW/Clang or `rasterfold.lib` with an MSVC-compatible linker. Keep `rasterfold.dll` on the application's normal DLL search path. Hosted static consumers link `librasterfold.a`, their own C runtime and the required Kernel32 import library. The archive does not override the caller's C memory functions. The DLL exports exactly the five functions and ordinals in [`src/rasterfold.def`](../src/rasterfold.def).

Android applications link the library for their ABI with the matching NDK. A JNI wrapper is application code; this repository supplies the C ABI and does not pretend to ship a Java or Kotlin package. Shared library loading and app lifecycle belong to the application.

## Errors and limits

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | Invalid API arguments or options |
| 2 | File I/O error, used by the CLI; the buffer-only API performs no I/O |
| 3 | Unsupported format, pixel layout or nonzero reserved option |
| 4 | Malformed image or file |
| 5 | Resource limit or allocation failure |

On failure, the output object is zeroed. Successful calls clear a supplied error object. Dimensions are limited to 32,768 per axis and 33,554,432 pixels; input files are limited to 256 MiB. Always check the return code before consuming output. Caller pointers and lengths must describe accessible memory, as with any C buffer interface.

The [encode](../examples/encode.c) and [decode](../examples/decode.c) examples show PPM file handling and ownership. They are demonstration programs; the production CLI adds flushed partial-file publication. `tests/test_api.py` covers API behavior and oracle fidelity, while `tests/test_artifacts.py` verifies exports and compiles/runs C and C++ consumers against shared and static libraries.

Current public API: 1.0. Current encoded format: 3. Image limits: 32768 pixels per dimension and 33554432 pixels total. These values are generated from the C headers.
